## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Samathavāra* ("How each offense is settled") is a chapter of the *Parivāra*, the procedural and analytical manual forming the final book of the Theravāda Vinaya Piṭaka. The text systematically analyzes the monastic rules by relating the various Vinaya offenses to the seven procedures for settling legal issues (*samatha* / *adhikaraṇa-samatha*). An English translation has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

Text-reuse analysis conducted by DharmaNexus indicates extensive overlap with other procedural and analytical sections of the *Parivāra*, registering 150 matching passages across 19 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its largest textual overlap is with the *Antarapeyyāla* (Pvr 4; 58 matches), along with other chapters treating the settlement of legal affairs, including other sections titled *Samathavāra* (such as Pvr 1.15, Pvr 1.7, and Pvr 2.7) and *Samathabheda* (Pvr 5) [DharmaNexus]. Beyond the Pali canon, DharmaNexus records automatic alignments between segments of this text and the Sanskrit *Prātimokṣasūtra* [DharmaNexus]. None of the secondary literature passages in the research dossier directly discuss this specific chapter, referring instead to serenity meditation (*samatha*), the *Samatha-khandhaka* of the *Cullavagga*, or the author Śamathadeva.

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
